newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency moans over stones in US barley cargo.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency moans over stones in US barley cargo.

text.p: Japan's Food Agency said on Thursday it had found stones in a shipment of U.S. barley and hinted it might shift to Canadian barley unless the problem was solved.
The stones were found in barley that arrived in mid-September. "Local feed makers are expressing concerns about the inspection system in the U.S.," an agency official said.
"If U.S. exporters fail to solve this, we may have to shift to other exporters such as Canada."
The stones, found in several different cargoes on the same ship, were up to 10 cm long, exceeding a limit set by the agency, the official said.
Japan imported 468,693 tonnes of barley in calendar 1995, mainly for use as a feed grain. Most came from Canada and the United States.

A barley trader in Tokyo said the stones probably got into the barley when it was harvested. "U.S. barley prices are increasingly competitive against that from Canada, but the discovery of stones in cargoes can damage its image," he said.
The Food Agency is the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry. In Japan, wheat and barley imports are handled solely by the agency, which carries out a weekly grain import tender.
